A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same neural-network reduction work by Ladner and Althoff. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and references support comparison despite extensive revision. Neither contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original verification rates, neuron reductions, and timings on MNIST and CIFAR-10 benchmarks, including Table 1 and Figures 4–11.

after.justification: Section V reports original image-benchmark experiments and adds compression, ACAS Xu verification, and quadrotor controller-reuse results, including Table II and Figures 15–16.

M1.justification: V1 describes adaptive tolerance reduction around its merging algorithm. V2 introduces binary-search tolerance selection for a target remaining-neuron ratio (Algorithm 1), sound input-compression preprocessing (Algorithm 3), and network-reuse procedures. Its revised on-the-fly algorithm also omits v1 Algorithm 1's bound-intersection step.

E1.justification: The MNIST and CIFAR-10 coverage, including ERAN, MNISTFC, Marabou, and Cifar2020, is retained. V2 adds verification of an ACAS Xu collision-avoidance property and a QUAD closed-loop controller scenario, substantially extending evaluation beyond image classification.

E2.justification: Comparator changes concern internal variants: the Cifar2020 comparison drops static merging (v1 Figure 11 versus v2 Figure 14), while v2 Figure 15 compares compression preprocessing against normal reduction. DeepAbstract and INNAbstract comparisons use cited results rather than newly executed external baselines.

E3.justification: V2 changes the default feed-forward setting from dynamic to static buckets and normalizes convolutional-network inputs; v1 explicitly leaves CIFAR-10 unnormalized. MNISTFC's stated radius/tolerance changes from 0.001/0.005 to 0.01/0.01. V2 also introduces target-ratio sweeps, ACAS Xu sensitivity-based splitting, and a specified reachable-set enlargement protocol for controller reuse.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled timing-versus-reduction curves, an output-bound sensitivity case study (Figure 10), compression-versus-normal reduction (Figure 15), and controller-reuse analysis (Figure 16). The ERAN tolerance sweep survives, while Cifar2020's static-versus-dynamic comparison becomes a perturbation-radius analysis.

E5.justification: V1 reports image averages and individual timing scatter points. V2 adds one-standard-deviation reduction error bars and timing bands, and specifies averaging ACAS Xu timing over 10 runs. These add descriptive variability reporting without establishing increased repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: ERAN table values are revised: at radius 0.001 and tolerance 0.005, sigmoid remaining neurons/verification rate change from 32.34%/96% to 33.36%/100%, under changed merging settings. New results include ACAS Xu retaining 61.33% of neurons with 4.21s versus 7.38s verification time, the compression example's 4.59s-to-0.78s timing reduction, and 60% controller reuse.

T1.justification: The original network-soundness result is retained as v2 Theorem 1 rather than newly introduced. V2 adds formal sound-compression and subset-reuse guarantees with proofs (Corollaries 1–2), along with convolutional-layer formalization and a derivation combining multiple buckets' approximation errors.

C1.justification: V2 retains sound on-the-fly merging and general activation support, but elevates automatic parameter selection, explicit convolutional-network reduction, and reuse into main contributions. It newly claims the first reduction approach explicitly addressing convolutional networks. The abstract replaces the specific below-5% reduction headline with a less specific fractional-reduction claim.

C2.justification: The central neuron-similarity explanation remains. V2 adds explanations for ReLU's weaker tolerance sensitivity and for aggressive early merging preventing later reductions. It also explicitly qualifies reuse by input-set containment and explains fallback to the original controller when that condition fails.

D1.justification: MATLAB, CORA, and hardware disclosures remain. V2 adds concrete tolerance-search initialization and expansion settings, documents an export interface and treatment of interval biases as additional inputs, and announces planned publication in the next CORA release. The PDFs do not establish that this release is already available.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands related work into a taxonomy of optimization, reachability, branch-and-bound, compression, and sound reduction. Added works include PRIMA, Beta-CROWN, and INNAbstract. It also develops explicit comparisons with prior reduction guarantees and introduces stronger positioning around convolutional-network reduction.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled around full automation and extensively rewritten. V2 separates Related Work and Contributions, expands the proof exposition, introduces an Applications section, and reorganizes evaluation around feed-forward networks, convolutional networks, and reuse instead of primarily grouping by dataset.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, rearranges the enclosure and merging diagrams, restructures the ERAN table, and replaces the timing scatter display with two curves and variability bands. It adds image-compression illustrations, output-bound and reachability plots, and the ACAS Xu table.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's sketch of adaptive tolerance selection, v2 supplies an explicit target-size search and formal support for compression and subset reuse. Experiments demonstrate these extensions beyond image classification, while variability reporting and expanded explanations make the tradeoffs easier to assess. Changed settings limit direct comparison of benchmark numbers, but the methodological specification and broader practical validation provide substantial overall gains.
